name: Waveshare RoArm-M2-S
description: A 4-DOF, ESP32-native desktop arm from Waveshare using ST3215 serial bus servos with metal internal gearing. "S" marks the standard-servo tier of the RoArm-M2 family, below the all-metal-case RoArm-M2-Pro. The Raspberry Pi visible in this unit's base is not a stock inclusion — Waveshare sells the arm and ESP32 driver board only, with the 40-pin header designed for a buyer-supplied Pi or Jetson.

specs.label: Controller
specs.note: runs web UI, ESP-NOW, JSON serial control standalone — no host computer required for basic use

specs.label: Servos
specs.note: nylon/fiberglass case, metal internal gearing, 12-bit magnetic encoder

specs.label: Repeatability
specs.note: load-tested figure; a separate "0.088°" spec is the servo encoder's resolution, not arm accuracy

specs.label: Compute Add-On
specs.note: not bundled; 40-pin header + camera mount bracket are provided for one

sourcing: Specs compiled from Waveshare's official product page and wiki, its GitHub organization (roarm_m2, waveshare_roarm_sdk, roarm_ws_em0 — including direct inspection of each repo's LICENSE file), and retailer listings (RobotShop, RobotPiShop, ThinkRobotics, CNX Software's coverage) as of this build. Independent long-form reviews are sparse for this specific model; the Raspberry Pi shown in the submitted photo is inferred to be a buyer-added component, not a stock inclusion — no official Waveshare bundle with a Pi included was found.

pricing.summary: Waveshare's own listing prices the RoArm-M2-S/M2-Pro pair at **$179.99–$299.99**; the base M2-S specifically runs roughly **$206–$260** across retailers (Amazon, AliExpress, RobotShop, RobotPiShop), with the all-metal-servo RoArm-M2-Pro upgrade running closer to **$330**. These figures cover the arm and ESP32 driver board only — no camera, no battery, and no Raspberry Pi or Jetson, all of which are separate purchases if you want the vision/ROS2 capabilities those add.

editorial.heading: Insights
editorial.body: Waveshare's often-repeated "0.088°" precision figure is actually the servo encoder's angular resolution, not measured arm repeatability — the real, load-tested spec Waveshare's current product page lists is **±4mm**. The core ESP32 firmware and Python SDK do carry genuine OSI-approved AGPL-3.0 licenses, but the separate ROS2/MoveIt2 workspace repo ships with no license file at all.
